1.why: Recovery tokens are bound to session.recovery.accountId and verified via tokenHash before reset uses that account.

2.why: The reset token lives only on the initiating session and is checked against that session's tokenHash, so it does not work for other users/sessions.

3.why: Password reset updates the account hash and consumes recovery but never invalidates or enumerates other entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS and non-HTTPS requests are rejected, though a minimum TLS version is not explicitly pinned.

5.why: Passwords use bcrypt and reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 digests; data are hashed rather than encrypted at rest.

6.why: There is no real email body; mock delivery only exposes the one-time code, not names or other private profile fields.

7.why: Inputs are validated (validReference/validToken/passwordError) and the UI inserts strings with textContent, not raw HTML.

8.why: Navigation is in-app hash routing and APIs do not accept user-controlled redirect URLs.

9.why: No email templates render user-supplied HTML or scripts; mock logs use plain text.

10.why: Recovery and MFA codes are written to the on-page logs panel and returned as mockToken/mockCode in API responses.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and not hardcoded, but issueMfa sets a fixed MFA code of "246810" in source.

12.why: The startup credential is randomToken(32) hashed at boot; no default password is accepted.

13.why: Login, recovery verify, and MFA each increment attempts and lock for LOCK_TTL after MAX_ATTEMPTS (5).

14.why: Recovery and login always return the same generic messages whether or not the identifier matches the mock account.

15.why: Reset tokens are randomBytes-based base64url values, stored hashed, and tied to the specific accountId on that session.
